title: Cursing out Lester Lanin over a demanded audition
summary: Sent by Jonah Jones for club dates, he told Lanin to look at Fats Waller records instead of auditioning, and later quit over slow payment.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Did you put in time with Lester Lanin too?

Naw, I did a couple -- (laughs). Only did a couple of things with Lester Lanin, but man, this will kill you. Jonah Jones, you know, when Jonah -- I told you we were friends years ago, and both of us starving to death, and he got a break, and so I ran into him, and I said look, throw some jobs my way. Give me a crumb or two. He said 'Okay, go down and see Lester Lanin and tell him I sent you.' And you get hooked up with this guy you've got a

chance to do two or three or four things a night, you know, a shot here, a shot there, and they'd take you in a car, and they'd bring you round, so I said oh, that'd be fine. So I went down to see Lester, and told him, My name's Herman Autrey, and Jonah Jones asked me to come down, and blah, blah, blah, blah. He said well, fine. Who'd you play with?

I said "well," said I've been recording with Fats for I don't know how many years. I said, "pick up any of his recordings, you'll see my name on it. I did it." Is that right? Well? Oh yes? Uh-huh. Who else? I said well, a heck of a lot of other people around New York I have recorded with. I say I'm on Decca, I'm on this, I'm on that. You know. Anyway. He said "would you come down and give me an audition?"
I said an audition? Yeah, come down to my office and bring your trumpet, and the -- and play away, well, just let me hear you. Well, I told him to go to hell.

I told him to bite me all over. I told him -- I don't know what the hell I didn't tell him, you know what I mean. I said you note playing son of a bitch, I called -- you know. You dirty (unintelligible). I just told you my name. You know -- everybody knows Fats Waller. I said now you can go buy you a record, and play it, drop a nickle in the juke box, I don't care what you do. You know, they -- good-bye! And I walked the hell out. So afterwards

I was working with -- some place, and two, three guys came in while I was playing, and he said well we -- Lester Lanin's lieutenants. I cursed him out. No, wait a minute, said we could use you. I said naw, you couldn't use me. So I said Lester forget it. (Unintelligible).

So I did a couple of things with Lester. Now I'm hot again because when you work for him, you've got to wait til a certain day to get paid. I don't know whether he -- something, you've got to go all the way down to the office, stand in line, and tell the girl your name, and she looks at the whole stack of checks, and well no, you have to come back tomorrow, maybe. Whatnot. You know, all that stuff. Big Chief Moore, and all them people. I said man, forget it. You know. Don't call me anymore. To hell with you.
So that was the end of your Lester Lanin --
Yeah, Lester Lanin, I mean piss on -- I mean (unintelligible).
Did you have any trouble while you did play for Lester, did you have any trouble adjusting to that style he has, that's just sort of continuous, the same --

Well, yes. I mean -- well I had played club dates before, and I knew what to expect. I knew what they -- what he liked, and they got -- has funny hats and stuff, and he was playing around there, but he wasn't there.
He sent me out on another one of these groups, you know. And I'd stay home, like who needs it, so I -- I didn't go on any of them.
No. I was looking -- I see it now.
So I didn't want to go anyway, so after that I said -- I tell him do me a favor. Don't call me.
